text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Yeltsin fires Lebed.
- Agreement in principle on "hot pursuit" in Hebron talks: joint Israeli, Palestinian pursuit.
- Army chief of staff rejects proposal he dismiss commander of force that was to rescue soldiers from Nablus's Joseph's Tomb during last month's clashes.
- Torah Judaism party demanding budget for religious buildings be increased tenfold.
- Treasury says chances growing capital reform package will be adopted after Bank of Israel governor backs taxes on savings.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Syria agrees to resume peace talks with Israel after negotiations with Palestinians finished.
- Revelation: Prime Minister Netanyahu's U.S. social security file.
- Israeli peace activist has light "brain incident".
- Mrs Netanyahu's former husband says he will not publish book about her.
- Nanny fired by Mrs Netanyahu brings suit for thousands of dollars in compensation.
MAARIV
- Syrian President Assad, Netanyahu exchange secret messages via intermediary.
- Interview with Bank Hapoalim chairman: No one knows what Netanyahu's economic policy is.
GLOBES
- Demand for foreign currency brings devaluation of one percent.
JERUSALEM POST
- Both sides say Hebron deal close.
- Netanyahu promises to advance Jewish settlement expansion plans.
- French foreign minister won't accompany Chirac to Israel to avoid running into dispute over a visit to Jerusalem PLO headquarters.
